headline: Council confirms Draper Laboratories tax, parking and land agreements in Hamilton Canal district.
summary: The deal covers Parcels 15 and 16 for the Draper Impact Center project. Building trades unions and the developers reached a labor agreement at 12:30 that day. It adds local hiring, apprenticeship, and workforce goals. The council also adopted a fiscal year 2027 minimum residential factor of 0.899590.
decisions: Approved canceling the City Council meetings of December 1st and December 29th, 2026, with 10 yeas.
Approved confirming executive session votes on Draper Laboratories parking, tax increment financing, and land agreements, with 10 yeas.
Approved the minimum residential factor for fiscal year 2027 at 0.899590, with 10 yeas.
Referred four gas and electric utility requests, including one at 61 Durant Street, to the wire inspector for report and recommendation.
Denied a substitute motion asking for a report on possible cannabis consumption lounges in Lowell.
Approved asking the city manager for a path to improve lighting in the Greenhalge School gymnasium.
Approved asking the city manager to arrange a discussion between the Lowell Housing Authority and the City Council.
Approved asking the city manager to install warning markers on newly created sidewalk extensions.
Approved asking the city manager to study turning on North Common Park basketball court lights an hour earlier.
Approved asking for a plan to prevent illegal dumping at the Cupples Square parking lot, with an update on security cameras.
Approved a $35,640 fire grant, a $75,000 MassDEP grant, and contracts with TEC, Inc., with 10 yeas.
Referred three MSBA loan orders for Bailey, McAuliffe, and Shaughnessy school projects to a public hearing on December 7th.
Referred the cemetery fee schedule ordinance to a public hearing on November 24th, 2026.
Referred three gas and electric petitions to a public hearing on November 24th, 2026, at 7:00 p.m.
discussion: Draper agreement enforceability: Public speakers said benefits listed in letters and packets are not legally enforceable. They asked for a community benefits agreement with binding terms.

Labor agreement: Building trades and the developers reached an agreement at 12:30 that day. The goals described at the meeting include 10% Lowell residents, 15.3% minority workers, 6.9% women, and apprenticeship requirements.

Cannabis consumption lounges: Some members raised concerns about cannabis potency and driving under the influence. Others said the city already allows cannabis sales and that lounges could be an economic development opportunity.
Environmental review: Public speakers asked that air emissions, wastewater, PFAS, heat, and noise impacts be evaluated and made public before agreements are approved.
Sewer capacity: The wastewater report said the treatment plant is at 100% of its daily allocated rate. The city will begin utility capacity meetings on Fridays.
